title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of daily stock prices, one price per day, in order. You may complete at most 2 buy-sell transactions total, where a transaction is one buy followed later by one sell. You must sell your current share before you can buy again, and you can never hold more than one share at a time.

**Return the maximum total profit achievable.**

You don't need to use both transactions if using fewer, or none, is more profitable.
constraints: at most 2 transactions are allowed, and you cannot hold more than one share at a time
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: buy at 0 (day 3) and sell at 3 (day 5) for a profit of 3, then buy at 1 (day 6) and sell at 4 (day 7) for a profit of 3, total 6
only one transaction is useful here: buy at 1, sell at 5, for a profit of 4
prices only fall, so the best choice is to make no transactions at all

code.Python3:
# Time:  O(n)
# Space: O(1)

class Solution(object):
    def maxProfit(self, prices):
        """
        :type prices: List[int]
        :rtype: int
        """
        hold1, hold2 = float("-inf"), float("-inf")
        release1, release2 = 0, 0
        for i in prices:
            hold1 = max(hold1, -i)
            release1 = max(release1, hold1 + i)
            hold2 = max(hold2, release1 - i)
            release2 = max(release2, hold2 + i)
        return release2

Consider two-pointer approaches if the array is sorted, or a sliding window if looking for contiguous subarrays.
Prefix sums or prefix XORs can answer range sum queries in O(1) time after O(N) preprocessing.
